paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: when God gives the plan, His people build exactly what He said. Look at how this passage ends. Bezalel son of Uri, of the tribe of Judah, "made everything that the LORD had commanded Moses" (Exodus 38:22). Every curtain, every clasp, every pole, and not one of them was somebody's bright idea.

And notice who built it. Bezalel led, Oholiab worked beside him, and the silver for those bases came from half a shekel from each man numbered, "a beka per person" (Exodus 38:26). Even the basin was made from the mirrors of the women who served at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting (Exodus 38:8). Nobody's gift was too small to end up in the house. I find that WILD, because I started out as a quarter in a bin!

So what do you do with that, baker? You get ready the way these folks did: you listen to what God has said, and then you do it. Revelation 19:7 says the bride "has made herself ready," and this is what ready looks like. It's ordinary, faithful work, one clasp at a time. The story isn't over, either, so keep that apron on.
